comment: sherpa-onnx reaches its own Java API through JNI, BY NAME: GetFieldID("model") on a config
object, FindClass("com/k2fsa/sherpa/onnx/WaveData") to hand a decoded recording back,
GetMethodID("invoke") on the progress callback we pass in. native-image keeps no name it
cannot see used, so an image that compiles and links still failed at the first spoken word.
Every type of the API jar is a data holder the C++ side reads or writes, so the whole package
is registered rather than the handful one code path happens to touch; sherpa_test.clj fails
when the jar carries a type this file does not, so bumping sherpa cannot silently drop one.
The MEMBERS under a type are the ones the C++ really looks up, captured with the tracing agent
over all three paths (piper, pocket-tts, parakeet). A type alone is NOT enough: JNI resolves a
field or a method, and one that is registered only as part of `allDeclared*` is not there to be
called - the image read an empty model path and then died inside the JNI trampoline instead of
throwing. Re-capture with -agentlib:native-image-agent after changing what we hand sherpa.
A member is named by its name and parameter types, which cannot tell a covariant method
from the synthetic BRIDGE beside it - and the bridge is the one JNI asks for by signature
(`next()Ljava/lang/Object;` on LinkedEntryIterator). A class that carries one is registered
whole with `allDeclaredMethods`; sherpa_test.clj fails when a member entry hides a bridge.
Two names here are not sherpa's. `GenerationCallback` is OURS - a deftype, because a reify's
class name is invented anew by every build and no metadata can name it. The JDK entries are what
sherpa's C++ asks for when it walks `GenerationConfig.extra` (a LinkedHashMap: ONE stable class,
where a Clojure map changes class with its size) and unwraps the Integer a callback returns.
